## Overview

Offline embedding refresh jobs are scheduled batch processes that regenerate vector embeddings for an entire corpus when the underlying embedding model changes or source documents are updated in bulk. Unlike on-demand embedding generation, these jobs run on a fixed cadence, re-embed the full or incremental document set, and swap the new vectors into the retrieval index atomically to prevent serving mixed-model results during the transition.

## Operational Pattern

The typical workflow:

1. **Trigger:** Model upgrade, bulk document ingest, or scheduled refresh cycle
2. **Batch regeneration:** Re-embed the full or incremental document set using the new (or updated) embedding model
3. **Atomic swap:** Replace the old embedding index with the new one in one operation
4. **Rollback readiness:** Stage the swap behind a blue/green index pattern to enable rapid rollback if quality degrades

## Key Operational Concerns

### Model Versioning
- Track and version the embedding model per batch run
- Document which model version produced which set of vectors
- Enable tracing of vector quality issues back to specific model versions

### Vector Drift Monitoring
- Measure drift between old and new embeddings for the same documents
- Monitor for unexpected changes that might indicate model regression or configuration drift
- Compare retrieval quality metrics before and after the swap

### Blue/Green Index Strategy
- Maintain two live indices (blue and green)
- Generate new vectors in the inactive index while serving from the active one
- Atomically switch traffic to the new index only after quality validation
- Roll back to the old index if quality regression is detected

## Benefits

- **Consistency:** All vectors use the same model at any given moment, avoiding mixed-model results
- **Atomicity:** Index swap is synchronous and all-or-nothing, preventing half-updated state
- **Rollback safety:** Blue/green pattern enables rapid rollback without affecting live queries
- **Predictability:** Fixed cadence allows predictable refresh windows and resource planning

## Related Concepts
